content.comment_body: Hello, I have a [product_name] [article_no] and I'm trying to connect it to my home network using a TP-Link Archer C8 router. I manually assigned an unused IP address to the [product_name]: IP: 192.168.1.153 Subnet mask: 255.255.255.0 (same as my PC, which is wired to the router) Gateway: 192.168.1.1 (same as my PC) When I access the router interface, I see all other devices but the [product_name] doesn't show up. The LAN LED on the [product_name] blinks green and orange. I also can't access the [product_name] with [product_name] software on my PC. Ping to 192.168.1.153 returns "Destination host unreachable." Any suggestions for getting it to communicate? Thanks in advance.

Welcome to the forum. Based on your description, the issue could be with your router or the network cable. I don't think the [product_name] itself is the problem. What is your PC's IP address? Try connecting the [product_name] directly to your PC, without going through the router.
If your router is acting as a DHCP server, try setting both your PC and the [product_name] to static IP addresses that are outside the DHCP range.

Thanks for the quick responses! Connecting the [product_name] directly to the PC works. The cable from [product_name] to router has been tested and is fine. I suspect I need to configure something in the router to enable communication. The router doesn't show the [product_name] in its device list, even though all other devices are visible. Pinging the [product_name] from my PC gives an "unreachable" message. My PC's IP is 192.168.1.154.

This question isn't really for this forum, as it's about your router and not a [company_name] product. What are you expecting—someone to read your router’s manual and guide you? You might be better off seeking help on a forum specific to the router manufacturer.

I see your point—I'm posting here because every other network device connects and communicates automatically. I haven't had issues with my router or standard TCP/IP devices. Theoretically, after connecting the [product_name], it should work like any other device, and I should access it from my PC on the same network. I wondered if there were special [product_name] communication settings for routers. I didn't mean to ask for router management help. My issue is with [product_name] communicating on the home network, and if anyone can help, I'd appreciate it. I think I'm missing a simple setting (port, IP config, etc.) to enable communication.

When you connect the PC directly to the [product_name], communication works, so the [product_name] is functioning properly. If adding the router causes issues, it's likely related to the router—maybe certain ports are blocked?
Which protocol are you using? IPv4 or IPv6? The [product_name] only supports IPv4.

Check your router settings and try reducing the LAN port speed from 1G to 100M where the [product_name] is connected. This solved my similar problem at home. There might be other parameters, but I didn't need to look further after adjusting the LAN speed.

I had a TP-Link router, and my devices only communicated when both the [product_name] and PC were set to a different IP range than the automatic settings. With automatic settings, I used 192.168.0.0, and with manual, I set 192.168.0.1. I always had to adjust my PC’s IP for things to work. After switching routers, the issue disappeared. I think it’s related to strict DMZ settings.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing challenges connecting a [product_name] module to a home network with a TP-Link router. The device does not appear in the router's list and cannot be reached from a PC over the network, although direct PC-to-[product_name] communication succeeds. Uncertainty remains about whether special network or [product_name] configurations are needed for basic connectivity, causing confusion over compatibility and settings.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] to join the home network via Ethernet and be accessible from their PC, just like standard TCP/IP devices, without requiring complex router or network configuration.
